note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A) beside C2/I-PROBLEMS: every expect and until is derived by hand from the wiring of Book I Answers 13, 14 and 15 (the only image-verified answers, programs.md N-5) and the Problem 13 and 14 statements, not printed. Same layout as the printed fixture: wires are Answer 13's list (cords 0-4); with power off the script disconnects them and connects Answer 14 (cords 5-8), then Answer 15 (cords 9-13). No erratum touches Answers 13-15 (ER-03 is prose for Problems 7 and 18). Derived checks taken from docs/plans/phase-5-step7-notes.md (I-PROBLEMS): Problem 13's converse (dial still and light 6 off with pushbutton 6 up, at power-on and after a run), and pushbutton 5 pushed while the dial is already turning under pushbutton 6 (Answers 14 and 15), then the dial staying still. Where the dial rests after a stop depends on the invented coast (O-R5), so the script does not assert it: after each stop it waits 600 ms, the operator sets the pointer knob by hand to a pad centre (dialGrab, a script choice), releases it, waits 600 ms and asserts the knob is still on that pad (more than one pad pitch at 25 rpm, so a turning dial cannot pass). Answer 14 stops by removing the drive (5Y leaves 5Z, 6X floats); Answer 15 stops by shorting STOP (5Y-5X joins D19 to D18) with RUN live, which rotary.md 3.2 condition 3 documents as a normal stop, so the breaker is expected ok. Not asserted: direction of rotation (the three answers share the polarity D17 +, D18 - but no direction is printed and the observable set has none, O-C14), the stop pad after any release (O-R5 coast), and Answers 1-12 and 16-20 (OCR only). Position untils encode motion only. Rotary geometry, run rate, coast and motor resistances remain profile fallbacks O-R1, O-R3 and O-R5.
